correctness.rationale: The coding problem is exactly the binary packing of 715 weight-nine 5-vectors, imposing one five-term ≤1 inequality for each of 495 weight-eight received vectors; the equivalent unit-transfer conflict graph has 4950 unordered edges. The checksum ≡0 mod 5 gives 143 valid codewords by cyclic symbol relabeling. The source two complete HiGHS MILP models report global dual upper bounds below 144; independently reconstructed all 715 vertices,495 output cliques,4950 conflict pairs and checksum validity. More importantly, an earlier published complete n=9 exact theorem gives the same conclusion. Numerical solver reports without a rational search certificate have a reproducibility/soundness limitation, not proof that the 143 bound is new.
